source_fields.question_text: How many distinct values can be obtained from <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> by inserting parentheses (no rearranging of factors)?
source_fields.explanation: Only the placement of the <math><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> changes the value. The four possibilities are <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn></math>, <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>126</mn></math>, <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>122</mn></math>, and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>121</mn></math>.

derived_fields.sub_skill: Counting distinct evaluation results under different parenthesizations; associativity awareness
derived_fields.problem_family: Parentheses placement and evaluation-order effects on mixed operations (multiplication and addition); counting distinct numeric outcomes from different binary tree parenthesizations
solve_strategy: Enumerate all structurally different full parenthesizations (binary trees) consistent with the given operand order that can change where the +1 is applied.
Identify which parenthesizations actually change the numerical effect of the +1 (i.e., whether +1 is inside some product factor or applied after all multiplications).
Evaluate each distinct relevant parenthesization numerically and collect distinct results.
Count distinct outcomes and map to appropriate answer choice.
derived_fields.reasoning_pattern: Case analysis over possible parenthesizations combined with application of associativity of multiplication and non-distributivity of addition over multiplication (so placing +1 inside a product changes the result).
logic_invariants: Multiplication is associative: grouping of pure products without addition does not change the product value.
Addition is not distributively equivalent to arbitrary regroupings: (a·b)+1 generally differs from a·(b+1).
Operands' order (sequence of factors) is fixed; only grouping (parentheses) may change evaluation order.
Distinct parenthesizations may lead to equal numeric results in special cases (e.g., zeros or ones), but with given operands they can be distinct.
changeable_parameters: Number of multiplicative factors before the +1 (length of factor chain).
Values of the multiplicative factors (positive integers, could include 0 or 1).
Position of the +1 relative to the chain (always at the end in this template, but could be inserted after other factors).
Type of operator used in the chain (e.g., multiplication, exponentiation) and position of the additive term.
Whether multiple additions are present instead of a single +1.
parameter_constraints: Operands' sequence must remain fixed (no reordering allowed).
Parentheses may be inserted only to change evaluation order; binary operation semantics apply.
For the typical problem flavor, factors are positive integers >1 to avoid degenerate equalities caused by 0 or 1.
Exactly one additive term (like +1) is present to keep the counting tractable unless intentionally varied.
derived_fields.answer_format: integer (count of distinct numeric values); for multiple-choice instances: option letter corresponding to that count
rendering_notes: Preserve original <math>...</math> MathML tags exactly in question text and choices.
When generating new variants, use MathML for inline numeric expressions to match source format.
Ensure parentheses are rendered clearly (use explicit parentheses in MathML when describing grouping).
risk_flags: Counting all Catalan-number parenthesizations instead of only those that change the location of the addition (overcount).
Assuming associativity of addition across multiplication (i.e., thinking grouping can't change value) — leads to undercounting.
Including degenerate parameter choices like 0 or 1 that collapse multiple parenthesizations to the same numeric result, changing answer key.
Misreading 'no rearranging of factors' and allowing commutativity to produce new orders.
